How to use the Storehouse Meal Planner V13

Approval requiredOrders from the bishops' storehouse must be approved by the bishop, through the elders quorum presidency or the Relief Society presidency.

This planner turns two weeks of meals into a filled-in Bishop's Order for Food and Supplies. You pick meals and servings; it scales every recipe, adds up the ingredients, rounds them to whole store packages, and writes the quantities onto the order form PDF.

Quick start

  1. Set People per meal and the First day at the top of the page.
  2. Turn on any filters you need, such as 🌾 Gluten-free or 🏪 Storehouse items only.
  3. Press Randomize all 14 days, or pick each meal yourself on the Plan tab.
  4. Change any meal you don't like, and adjust the servings boxes.
  5. Add diapers, toiletries or cleaning supplies on the Household items tab.
  6. Open the Order form tab, fill in the recipient details, check the quantities, and press Download filled order form (PDF).
  7. Enter the Reviewer email (a member of the elders quorum or Relief Society presidency) and press Send to reviewer so the order can go to the bishop for approval.
  8. Use the Recipes tab as your cook sheet for the two weeks.

Settings at the top of the page

People per meal
The default number of servings for every meal. Changing it updates every servings box that still had the old number; boxes you changed by hand stay as they are. It also fills the "# in household" box on the order form.
First day
The date of day 1. The planner shows 14 days from this date, labeled with weekday names, and prints the dates on the PDF menu page.
Show only
Diet filters, the storehouse-only switch and the ingredient exclusions. See Filters and exclusions below.
Randomize all 14 days
Fills every meal slot on all 14 days with recipes that match your filters. It replaces what was there.
Clear
Empties every meal slot. Press it twice; the first press asks you to confirm.
Save plan file / Open plan file
Save the whole plan (meals, servings, filters, household items and order details) to a file, and open it again later or on another device.

Planning meals (Plan tab)

Each day card has seven slots, in this order: Breakfast, Snack, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Side dish, Dessert.

  • Meal menus. Click a menu to choose a recipe. Recipes are grouped under Breakfasts, Lunches, Dinners, Side dishes, Snacks and Desserts. The group that matches the slot is listed first, but you can pick from any group, for example pancakes for dinner.
  • Icons after each name show which recipes are gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian or vegan, and which need items not on the order form. See Icons and colors.
  • Servings box. The number to the right of each menu is how many servings that meal makes. Set it to 0 to skip a meal without removing it.
  • Tags under a meal repeat the icons with words, and show Packs to go on lunches that travel well.
  • Randomize on a day card replaces just that day's meals. It tries not to repeat anything from the three days on either side.
  • Daily nutrition. The line at the bottom of each day estimates calories, protein, carbs, fat and sodium for one person eating one serving of each meal that day.

Last Night Left Overs

Every lunch menu (except day 1's) starts with Last Night Left Overs. Choose it when lunch will be the leftovers from the dinner the night before.

  • The lunch's servings are added to that dinner. If dinner is set to 4 and the next day's lunch is Last Night Left Overs with 4 servings, the dinner shows +4 for tomorrow's lunch · cook 8.
  • The cook sheet and the order form use the larger amount, so the ingredients for the extra servings are ordered.
  • If there is no dinner the night before, the lunch shows a warning.
  • The randomizers never choose Last Night Left Overs. A day's Randomize button replaces it with a regular lunch.

Filters and exclusions

🌾 Gluten-free, 🥕 Vegetarian, 🌱 Vegan, 🥛 Dairy-free
Show only recipes that meet every filter you turn on. Turning on Vegan also turns on Vegetarian. Filters apply to the meal menus, the recipe library and both randomizers. Meals already planned stay in place; ones that no longer fit are marked Excluded by your filters.
🏪 Storehouse items only
Hides every recipe that needs something not on the Bishop's Order, such as taco seasoning, soy sauce or plant milk.
🚫 Exclude ingredients
Opens a checklist of every ingredient, grouped like the order form. Check an ingredient to hide every recipe that uses it, for an allergy, a dislike, or an item the storehouse is out of. Use the search box to find an ingredient fast, Clear all to reset, and Done to close the list. The button shows how many ingredients are excluded.

Tip: after changing filters, press Randomize all 14 days to rebuild the plan with them.

Recipes tab

  • This plan's cook sheet lists every planned meal, day by day, with the recipe already scaled to the servings you set, including any extra for leftover lunches. Click a meal to open it, or use Open all and Close all.
  • All recipes is the full library of 300+ recipes. Search by recipe name or ingredient, pick a meal type, and change the serves box on any recipe to rescale it.
  • Each recipe shows ingredients, steps, and estimated nutrition per serving: calories, protein, carbs, fat, fiber and sodium.
  • Amounts in the ingredient list are scaled. Any amounts written inside the steps are for the recipe's original size, which is noted under the steps.

Household items tab

Enter quantities for the non-food lines on the Bishop's Order: baby products, household products and personal products. Whatever you enter goes onto the Order form tab, the CSV and the filled PDF. The tab shows a count of the units you've entered.

Order form tab

  • Order details. These print on the PDF:
    • Recipient, # in household and Address print in the form's header.
    • Member email prints on the "Notify via Email" line and checks that box.
    • Member phone number prints on the "Notify via Text" line and checks that box.
    • Reviewer email is the elders quorum or Relief Society presidency member who reviews the order. It prints on the menu page and is used by Send to reviewer.
    • Instructions to storehouse and recipient print in the instructions area.
  • Send to reviewer builds the filled order form PDF and sends it toward your reviewer:
    • On an iPhone or Android phone, the share menu opens with the PDF attached and a message ready. Choose Mail, Gmail or Messages, enter or pick the reviewer's address, and send.
    • On a computer, your email program opens with the reviewer's address, subject and message filled in. Attach the PDF that was just downloaded, then send.
    • Every time you send, a copy of the PDF is also downloaded to your device for your records.
    • If no email opens, a box below the button shows the address, subject and message with Copy buttons, so you can paste them into any email.
    • The planner never sends email by itself; you always press Send in your own email app.
  • Order summary. Meals planned, form lines, total units ordered, and how many items to buy separately.
  • Food items. For each line on the form: the package size, how much the recipes need, and the quantity to order. Quantities add every planned meal together, then round each item up to whole packages.
  • Adjusting quantities. Type over any quantity to change it, for example if the family already has rice at home. Changed numbers are highlighted; press reset to go back to the calculated amount. Randomizing clears your changes.
  • Show every food line on the form lists the lines the plan doesn't use, so you can order extras by hand.
  • Household and personal items repeats what you entered on the Household items tab.
  • Not on the Bishop's Order — buy separately lists the extra items the plan needs, why each is there, how much the recipes need, and how many packages to buy.
  • Download filled order form (PDF) creates the official two-page form with every quantity filled in, plus extra pages with the two-week menu, the buy-separately list and the disclaimer.
  • Download list (CSV) creates a spreadsheet file of the same order.

Saving, sharing and phones

  • Your plan saves automatically in the browser you're using. It stays there when you close the page, but it isn't shared with other people, other browsers or other devices.
  • To move or share a plan, press Save plan file and send the file. The other person opens it with Open plan file.
  • Online version (the claude.ai link): works on computers and phones. People you share it with need a Claude account. On an iPhone, downloads open the share sheet so you can save to Files or send the PDF.
  • Standalone file (Storehouse Meal Planner V13.html): works offline in any computer browser and on Android phones in Chrome. Previews inside phone apps (Gmail, Google Drive, Messages, Files, Mail, the Claude app) only show the layout and don't run the planner.
  • Android (Pixel, Samsung and others): download the file, open the Files app, tap the file, and choose Open with Chrome. If it opens in a viewer that only shows the layout, use Open with Chrome from that viewer's menu.
  • iPhone and iPad: use the online link. iPhones can't open a saved HTML file in full Safari.
  • The version number next to the title, in the footer and on the PDF tells you which edition you're using.

Common questions

Why does the order have more than the recipes need?
Items come in whole packages. If the recipes need 1¼ bags of rice, the order is 2 bags.
A recipe I want isn't in the menu.
A filter or an excluded ingredient is probably hiding it. Turn filters off or clear the exclusions.
How do I plan for a different number of people at one meal?
Change that meal's servings box. Only that meal changes.
Does the planner email the order for me?
No. Send to reviewer prepares the email or share message and attaches or downloads the PDF, but you press Send in your own email or messaging app. Member and reviewer details stay on your device.
Can I skip a meal?
Choose "— none —" or set its servings to 0.
How accurate is the nutrition?
It's an estimate from typical package values. Brands, portions and preparation change it.
Please noteNutrition information is an estimate based on typical package values and will vary with brands, portion sizes and preparation. Gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian and vegan labels are a guide only: check every ingredient label and confirm a recipe is safe for you before eating, especially for food allergies or celiac disease.
